To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the drivers' preferences are dynamic and can be modeled by two types of features, which help to improve the drivers' earning efficiency.

1) the drivers' preferences are dynamic over time, 2) the drivers' preference changes can be characterized into three categories: self improving, experienced and exploring, 3) the drivers' self-improvement can be explained by adjusting preferences to habit features, and 4) the drivers' stable preference can be explained by keeping preferences to profile features.
we establish a Dynamic Human Preference Analytics framework, and apply it to the taxi driver learning process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of taxi drivers' preference learning and the effects on their earning efficiency.
understanding human behaviors in the real world.
the dynamics of drivers' preferences and the effects on their learning process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
drivers tend to keep their preferences to profile features stable while keep adjusting the preferences to habit features.
the learning process of a driver can be characterized as a process from exploring to exploiting and then self improving.
the drivers' preference dynamics are closely associated with the drivers' learning curves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
drivers with better working efficiency tend to keep adjusting the preferences to habit features.
the taxi drivers' working preferences can be learned and analyzed with our DHPA framework.
drivers with different characteristics learn different preferences.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dynamic human preference analytics framework can be applied to many other real world sequential human decision making processes, which can help to better understand the human decision making process and improve their efficiency.

we can characterize the dynamics of taxi drivers' preferences over time and understand the drivers' learning curves, which is useful in the taxi operation management and other sequential decision making processes.
the dynamic preference analysis can help to understand human learning process, and can be applied to many real-world applications such as human resource management, marketing, etc.
